chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had upon him the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), alone. So he circumambulated five circuits from it, then his belly was struck (with pain). So he feared that he might be caught by surprise (by the pain or death), so he went out to his house, so he relieved himself (from urine/stool), then he had intercourse with his slave girl.

He (peace be upon him) said: He should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate the House (Kaaba) with two circuits, completing what had remained upon him from his circumambulation, and he should seek forgiveness of Allah, and he should not repeat (the full seven circuits).

And if it was the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), so he had circumambulated three circuits from it, then went out and had intercourse, so he has spoiled his Hajj, and upon him is a Badatah (a camel), and he should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate a full week (seven circuits).

key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Circumambulation of the women (referring to the specific act of intercourse during Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who has intercourse with his slave girl during Hajb depending on the number of remaining circuits?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'partial invalidation' in Hajj rituals, where the severity of the penalty depends on the proportion of rituals already completed before the act of intercourse. It highlights the scholarly distinction between a pilgrim who retains the validity of his Hajj by completing the remaining circuits versus one whose Hajj is nullified, requiring a camel (badanah) as expiation and a full repetition of the Tawaf. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the integrity of ritual sequence and the specific conditions under which minor defects do not void the entire pilgrimage.
